experiment: Force the cross-attention gate open (gate_init=1.0 instead of the provable-no-op default 0.0) -- does the graph pathway help when given the chance, not just observed to never open on its own?
pass_mark: descriptive only, n=3 vs n=3 not statistically conclusive on its own (disclosed before running, same as the random-edge ablation)
finding: Gates stayed open throughout training in all 3 seeds (final values ~1.0-1.03, never drifted back toward zero) -- the zero-init gate never opening on its own is NOT the model actively suppressing the pathway, it simply never had a reason to move. But an open, stable gate produces essentially identical Dice to a closed one (mean diff +0.0003). The graph pathway carries no useful information for segmentation accuracy regardless of how much of it is allowed through.
